Any other field (including `status` and `scheduledAt`) is rejected with **400** and `unsupportedFields` listing what was sent. **To edit a post — including moving a draft to `scheduled` — use `PUT /api/posts/{id}` with `{ "status": "scheduled", "scheduledAt": "<future ISO 8601>" }`.** Requires a role that can edit posts (owner, admin, approver, contributor); viewers get 403 FORBIDDEN.

assignedUserId.description: The member expected to act on this post next, or null to unassign. Must be a member of the organization (422 otherwise). Deliberately not on PUT: that is the full-document save, and it would clear an assignment a teammate made while the post was open in an editor.

ifUnmodifiedSince.description: Optional precondition: the post's `updatedAt` as you last read it, ISO 8601 with milliseconds. The edit is refused with 409 CONFLICT if somebody else has changed the post since then, instead of overwriting their version. Omit it for the previous behaviour, last write wins. Milliseconds matter — two edits in the same second are distinct, which is why this is a body field and not the If-Unmodified-Since header.

recurringScheduleId.description: Repeat-schedule id to attach, or null to detach.

400.description: A field other than recurringScheduleId or ifUnmodifiedSince was sent; use PUT instead

409.description: Somebody else changed the post after the ifUnmodifiedSince you sent. The error body carries the post's current updatedAt.

422.description: assignedUserId is not a member of this organization

patch.summary: Attach or detach a post's recurring schedule

put.description: Update a draft, scheduled, failed, or partial post. Note: the per-platform object fields (platformSpecific, platformContent, postTypeOverrides, platformThreadParts) are replaced wholesale, not merged — send the complete object including keys for every platform you want to keep. Sending a partial object (e.g. only one platform's content) removes the stored values for all other platforms. Editing a FAILED post silently resets its status to draft and clears its failed platform results (they revert to pending). Editing a PARTIAL post keeps it partial and leaves every platform row untouched — it is live on some channels; re-send the failed ones with POST /api/posts/{id}/retry, or send status 'scheduled' with a scheduledAt, which re-queues exactly the failed channels for that time. Platforms in 'published', 'processing', or 'unconfirmed' are never reset by an edit. When `channels` is sent, rows for channels that remain keep their state (a published channel is NOT re-published on the next publish); removed channels are dropped and new ones added as pending. A channel whose destination has already gone out (status `published`, `publishing`, `processing` or `unconfirmed`) cannot be left out: the request is refused with 400 `CHANNEL_ALREADY_PUBLISHED` before anything is saved, and `error.channelIds` lists the channels concerned. The post stays live on those platforms either way; keep them in the list. Send the optional status field ('draft' or 'scheduled') to move a post between draft and scheduled; other status values are rejected. To publish immediately, use POST /api/posts/{id}/publish instead. Requires a role that can edit posts (owner, admin, approver, contributor); viewers get 403 FORBIDDEN.

channels.description: Full target channel list ({ channelId, platform } items). Rows for channels already on the post are kept with their current publish state; removed channels are deleted; new channels are added as pending. A channel that has already published (or may have: `publishing`, `processing`, `unconfirmed`) must stay in the list, or the request is refused with 400 `CHANNEL_ALREADY_PUBLISHED` and nothing is saved.

ifUnmodifiedSince.description: Optional precondition: the post's `updatedAt` as you last read it, ISO 8601 with milliseconds. The edit is refused with 409 CONFLICT if somebody else has changed the post since then, instead of overwriting their version. Omit it for the previous behaviour, last write wins. Milliseconds matter — two edits in the same second are distinct, which is why this is a body field and not the If-Unmodified-Since header.

linkTrackingOverride.description: Per-post override for link tracking (bulkpubli.sh). `true` forces links in this post to be shortened and their clicks counted, `false` forces them to publish as written, and `null` (the default) inherits the organization's Link Tracking setting. Shortening happens at publish time, per channel, so two accounts on the same platform get distinct codes; it is skipped for a channel when the rewrite would push the post past that platform's character limit. Short links are part of the Pro and Business plans: on Free, links always publish as written and `true` has no effect.

platformContent.description: Per-platform content overrides, keyed by platform; values must be plain strings (nested objects are rejected with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR). Replaced wholesale on update.

platformSpecific.description: Per-platform options, keyed by platform. Replaced wholesale on update (not merged). Accepts the same per-platform options and validation as `platformSpecific` on `POST /api/posts`.

postTypeOverrides.description: Per-platform post type overrides, keyed by platform. Replaced wholesale on update. LinkedIn accepts post, multi_image, pdf_carousel, article, document, poll and reshare; the `document`, `poll` and `reshare` types and a document attached to a non-LinkedIn channel are described on POST /api/posts. `repost` (X, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon) reposts an existing post at the scheduled time: the post's own text and media are ignored and `platformSpecific.<platform>.repostId` must hold the target (X: status URL or ID; Mastodon: status URL or ID; Bluesky: bsky.app post URL or at:// URI; Threads: the numeric post ID; Threads links cannot be used, and for posts published through BulkPublish the ID is in the post details). A missing or unparsable target is rejected with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. This post type is available through the API only; the composer in the app does not offer it.

publishWhenApproved.description: Optional. See POST /api/posts. An explicit value is stored while the post waits for approval. When omitted, it is kept, except that giving the post a different scheduledAt clears it to false (a picked time is not "as soon as possible"), and it is always false once the post no longer has approvalStatus 'pending' (approving or rejecting it clears it too). When an approved post goes back for review, it starts from false unless this request sets it. Must be a boolean (400 VALIDATION_ERROR otherwise).

requestApproval.description: Optional. Set true to hold a scheduled post for team approval (approvalStatus becomes 'pending'). Forced on server-side for roles without post:publish (contributors), regardless of this flag.

status.description: Move the post between draft and scheduled. Setting 'scheduled' requires a future scheduledAt (in this body or already stored) and at least one channel; setting 'draft' unschedules it. Any other value is rejected. Omit to leave the status unchanged (a failed post still auto-resets to draft on edit; a partial post stays partial). Setting 'scheduled' on a partial post re-queues its failed channels only; published channels are not re-sent. To publish immediately, use POST /api/posts/{id}/publish instead.

threadParts.description: Thread segments (required when postFormat is 'thread'; at least 2). Each part: { content, mediaFileIds }. EVERY part is measured against the character limit of every platform the post targets, not just the first one — a part over the limit is rejected with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR naming the part number, the platform and its limit. URLs count the way the platform counts them (23 characters on X and Mastodon).

400.description: Validation error, including `CHANNEL_ALREADY_PUBLISHED` when `channels` leaves out a channel the post has already gone out on

409.description: Somebody else changed the post after the ifUnmodifiedSince you sent. The error body carries the post's current updatedAt.

post.description: Requires a role with post:approve (owner, admin, approver). Releases a post with approvalStatus 'pending': it publishes at its scheduled time, or immediately if that time passed less than 15 minutes ago. If the scheduled time passed more than 15 minutes ago, the optional body field whenLate decides: 'publish' publishes it immediately (the response has status 'publishing'); 'hold' approves it but does not publish it: it comes back with status 'draft' (approvalStatus 'approved', scheduledAt unchanged) and the author is notified to choose a new time. When whenLate is omitted it follows the post's publishWhenApproved: true means 'publish', false means 'hold'. whenLate has no effect on a post whose time is still ahead or passed less than 15 minutes ago. The author is notified in-app either way. The body is optional; an empty body behaves like {}. Approving sets publishWhenApproved to false. Send ifUnmodifiedSince to make sure you approve the version you reviewed.

ifUnmodifiedSince.description: Optional. The post's updatedAt as you last loaded it. When sent, the post is approved only if it has not changed since; otherwise nothing is written and you get 409 CONFLICT with the current updatedAt in error.updatedAt, so you never approve (and publish) an edit you have not seen. Must be an ISO 8601 timestamp (400 VALIDATION_ERROR otherwise). Omit it to approve whatever version is current.

whenLate.description: What to do if the post's scheduled time passed more than 15 minutes ago: 'publish' = publish now, 'hold' = approve and return it to draft for the author to pick a new time. Defaults to 'publish' when the post's publishWhenApproved is true, otherwise 'hold'. Any other value is rejected with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

400.description: Post is not awaiting approval, whenLate is not 'publish' or 'hold', or ifUnmodifiedSince is not an ISO 8601 timestamp

409.description: The post changed since you loaded it (only checked when ifUnmodifiedSince is sent; error.updatedAt then carries the current value), or it is no longer awaiting approval because someone else approved, rejected or withdrew it first. Nothing was written. Reload it and review again.

post.description:
Acts on a comment, on the platform, as the channel the post was published to. `like`/`unlike` and `hide`/`unhide` can be undone; **`delete` is permanent on the platform** and needs a role that can publish (owner, admin, approver) — other roles get 403. Which actions a channel supports is in `commentActions` on its `GET /api/posts/{id}/engagement` entry; anything else returns 422. Returns per-platform lists of the people/pages who commented on or reacted to a published post — with name, handle/headline, profile photo and profile URL when the platform exposes them.

Ten of the fifteen platforms return engagement: Facebook, Instagram, X, LinkedIn, YouTube, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon, Discord and Tumblr. Platforms that expose commenters but never individual likers (Instagram, YouTube, Threads) populate `comments` only and set `reactionsUnsupported: true` plus an explanatory `notice`.

Exactly five platforms have no comment API at all and return `unsupported: true` with a `notice` saying why: **TikTok** (comments are Research-API only), **Pinterest** (v5 exposes no Pin comments), **Google Business** (local posts have no comment surface; reviews attach to the location, not the post), **Telegram** (a bot learns of comments only through pushed updates, so they cannot be read on request) and **Snapchat** (the Public Profile API reports reply counts only, never individual comments).

Platforms in 'unconfirmed' are never touched here — if they are the only rows left the request fails with **400** `code: "UNCONFIRMED_REQUIRES_REPUBLISH"`; check the account, then use POST /api/posts/{id}/retry with `republish: true`.
